entries.reason: WHEN OTHER is a CEEDAYS feedback token that is none of the nine CSUTLDTC names. IBM documents the whole set: z/OS Language Environment Programming Reference (V2R2 edition), CEEDAYS, 'The following symbolic conditions can result from this service' (p. 245), lists CEE000 and the eight severity-3 conditions CEE2EB 2507, CEE2EC 2508, CEE2ED 2509, CEE2EH 2513, CEE2EL 2517, CEE2EM 2518, CEE2EO 2520, CEE2EP 2521. These are exactly the nine 88-levels of FEEDBACK-TOKEN-VALUE (lines 62-70 of CSUTLDTC), so no documented condition falls through. The IBM i copy of the service (ssw_ibm_i_73 apis/CEEDAYS.htm) adds only CEE0501 / CEE0502 (operational descriptor data type not valid / missing) and CEE9902 (unexpected user error); those are argument-shape or internal failures, and A000-MAIN passes four fixed items (WS-DATE-TO-TEST, WS-DATE-FORMAT, OUTPUT-LILLIAN, FEEDBACK-CODE) with no operational descriptors. The model (Ceedays.java, ceedays.c) returns only 0, 2507, 2508, 2513 and 2520, each a listed arm. Assumption: CEEDAYS raises only its documented conditions; a token outside them would be undocumented IBM behaviour (the reason is IBM's documented set, not a z/OS run).

FC-INSUFFICIENT-DATA (CEE2EB, 2507) needs a date shorter than the picture's span. A000-MAIN sets VSTRING-LENGTH OF WS-DATE-TO-TEST to LENGTH OF LS-DATE (line 108, a PIC X(10) LINKAGE item, always 10) and the longest picture CEEDAYS is modelled for spans 10 (YYYY-MM-DD); every caller (COTRN02C, CORPT00C: 'YYYY-MM-DD'; CSUTLDPY: 'YYYYMMDD') passes a constant picture of span 8 or 10, so the date is never shorter. Ceedays.java and ceedays.c do return 2507; only this program cannot reach it.

FC-INVALID-ERA (CEE2ED, 2509) is raised for an era name in the date string, which needs an era picture (JJJJ / ERA). Every caller of CSUTLDTC passes a constant numeric picture ('YYYY-MM-DD' in COTRN02C and CORPT00C WS-DATE-FORMAT, 'YYYYMMDD' in CSUTLDPY), and the oracle refuses an era picture by name, so no run reaches it.

FC-INVALID-MONTH (CEE2EL, 2517) is the message for a month not recognized. IBM's documentation does not say what a numeric month outside 1-12 is; the owner ruled 2026-10-29 that it is CEE2EC (2508, date value not valid), recorded as ASSUMED in register L1 (not z/OS calibration). Under that ruling the model never raises 2517 for a numeric picture, and every caller of CSUTLDTC (COTRN02C and CORPT00C 'YYYY-MM-DD', CSUTLDPY 'YYYYMMDD') passes one; a month name needs a month-name picture, which the oracle refuses by name. The month-13 date itself is run (carddemo-dateutil month-13, month-00) and takes the 2508 arm.

FC-BAD-PIC-STRING (CEE2EM, 2518) needs a picture string IBM rejects. Every caller passes a constant, valid numeric picture (COTRN02C / CORPT00C 'YYYY-MM-DD', CSUTLDPY 'YYYYMMDD'); a picture the oracle does not model is refused by name (exit 98), never answered, so no run reaches it.

FC-YEAR-IN-ERA-ZERO (CEE2EP, 2521) is raised for a year of zero in an era-based date (era picture). Every caller passes a numeric Gregorian picture with YYYY, where year 0000 is outside the supported range (2513, taken by the year-zero scenario); an era picture is refused by the oracle by name, so no run reaches it.
